metadata.source: Yamaha 2015 Europe R1/R1M launch specifications and service manual; Yamaha 2016 kit manual STD cam centres; APE 2017 R1 valve data as a same-generation proxy. Remaining estimates originally from engine-sim yzf_r1.mr (MIT, Copyright 2022 Ange Yaghi)
metadata.notes: 2015 unrestricted Europe reference: 79.0 x 50.9 mm, 998 cc, compression 13.0, 147.1 kW at 13500 rpm and 112.4 Nm at 11500 rpm. Primary 1.634, final 2.563, 200 kg curb mass plus separate rider. Valve heads 33/26.5 mm are nominal service-manual dimensions; four 45 mm throttle bores. Yamaha STD cam centres 108 ATDC / 110 BTDC correspond to simulation phases 468/250. APE 2017 same-generation R1 lists 9.7/8.8 mm valve lift and 284/280 degrees duration at 0.15/0.25 mm; used as a proxy, not a verified 2015 cam trace. Generic seat ramps remain an approximation. Runner equivalent bore 45 mm is an ESTIMATE based on throttle bore, not a measured port dimension; fixed 0.25 m length and 50 cc effective port volume remain estimates and do not reproduce YCC-I switching. Clutch capacity 200 Nm is an estimated crank-side holding capacity (not a measured spring/plate value), replacing the 99.8 Nm fallback below the published engine torque. Drag area 0.35 m2 represents a tucked rider, using the older R1 CFD example in Limebeer and Sharma, BMD2010 p48, as a proxy; it is not verified 2015 R1M aero data. Flywheel, rod ratio, limiter and heat transfer remain estimated. Crossplane intervals 270/180/90/180. Real-world power, speed and transient acceptance remains incomplete. Sources: https://global.yamaha-motor.com/news/2014/1104/yzf-r1.html ; https://www.manualslib.com/manual/1176112/Yamaha-Yzf-R1.html?page=4 ; https://www.aperaceparts.com/tech/2017yzfr1_1.html ; https://www.bicycle.tudelft.nl/ProceedingsBMD2010/BookAbstractsBMD2010.pdf
